authors: de Araujo, Antonio C.B.; Govatsmark, Marius; Skogestad, Sigurd
title: Application of plantwide control to the HDA process. I - steady-state optimization and self-optimizing control
verified_fact: Bibliographic record confirmed in Crossref (authors, 2007, title, journal). Facts read in the authors' submitted manuscript (https://skoge.folk.ntnu.no/publications/2007/araujo_hda_part1_cep/old-submitted/HDASubmission.pdf, preprint dated 30 Oct 2006): HDA process 'first presented in a contest which the American Institute of Chemical Engineers arranged' (McKetta, 1977); 'Douglas (1988) used another version of the HDA process to demonstrate a steady-state procedure for flowsheet design'; reactions 'Toluene + H2 -> Benzene + Methane' and '2 Benzene <-> Diphenyl + H2'; adiabatic plug-flow reactor; effluent 'quenched by a portion of the recycle separator liquid flow to prevent coking'; purge 'to avoid accumulation of methane within the process'; toluene column separates unreacted toluene from diphenyl and recycles it; constraints: H2/(benzene+toluene+diphenyl) >= 5 'to prevent coking', reactor inlet pressure <= 500 psia, reactor outlet T <= 1300 F, quencher outlet T <= 1150 F, reactor inlet T >= 1150 F; fresh gas 97% hydrogen / 3% methane; Table 7 'Economic data for the HDA process based on Douglas (1988)': benzene 9.04 $/lbmol, toluene 6.04 $/lbmol, fresh gas 1.32 $/lbmol, fuel 4.00e-6 $/Btu; 8150 h/y; by-products purge, stabilizer distillate and toluene-column bottoms sold as fuel; Wolff (1994) 'concluded that the HDA process is controllable provided the instability of the heat-integrated reactor is resolved'; Aspen model stream table: reactor inlet 1201.2 F and outlet 1277.2 F at 500 psi, fresh toluene 300 lbmol/h, benzene product 268 lbmol/h, diphenyl bottoms 8 lbmol/h. Basis year of prices not stated in the paper. Further facts read in the same manuscript: distillate specification, benzene mole fraction of at least 0.9997; separator temperature limited to 95-105 F; steam price 2.50e-6 $/Btu; the feed is heated against the reactor effluent (feed-effluent heat exchange); objective function, economic potential (product and by-product fuel value minus feed, fuel, cooling water, power and steam costs); nominal optimum profit 4,693.4 k$/year at fresh toluene 300 lbmol/h; the HDA process 'has been exhaustively studied' for design, controllability and control structure selection.

verified_fact: 'The homogeneous reactions take place in the range 600 C - below this temperature the reaction rate is too slow - to 700 C - above this temperature a significant amount of hydrocracking takes place - and at a pressure of about 35 bar. 'the methane, which is produced in the reaction and enters as an impurity in the hydrogen stream, will accumulate in the gas-recycle loop. title: PubChem Compound Summary for CID 241, Benzene
container: PubChem, U.S. National Library of Medicine, National Institutes of Health
verified_fact: Methods of Manufacturing: 'Benzene is produced from the hydrodemethylation of toluene under catalytic or thermal conditions. The main catalytic hydrodealkylation processes are Hydeal and DETOL. Two widely used thermal processes are HDA and THD. These processes contribute 25-30% of the world's total benzene supply.' Catalytic: 'usually supported chromium or molybdenum oxides, platinum or platinum oxides, on silica or alumina. The operating temperatures range from 500 to 595 C and pressures are usually 4-6 MPa (40-60 atm). The reaction is highly exothermic and the temperature is controlled by injection of quench hydrogen at several places along the reaction. Conversions per pass typically reach 90% and selectivity to benzene is often >95%. The catalytic process occurs at lower temperatures and offers higher selectivities but requires frequent regeneration of the catalyst.' 'Worldwide, ~30% of commercial benzene is produced by catalytic reforming'; 'Approximately 30-35% of benzene produced worldwide is derived from pyrolysis gasoline'; transalkylation/disproportionation 'Economic feasibility ... depends on the relative prices of benzene, toluene, and xylene ... In recent years, xylene and benzene prices have generally been higher than toluene prices so transalkylation is presently an attractive alternative to hydrodealkylation.' (undated text). U.S. Production (EPA CDR, via HSDB): 2023: 15,000,000,000 - <20,000,000,000 lb; 2022: 10,000,000,000 - <15,000,000,000 lb; 2021 and 2020: 15,000,000,000 - <20,000,000,000 lb. IARC: Group 1, carcinogenic to humans (Vol 100F, 2012; Vol 120, 2018). OSHA 1910.1028: TWA 1 ppm, STEL 5 ppm. ACGIH TLV: 0.5 ppm TWA, 2.5 ppm STEL, skin, A1 confirmed human carcinogen. Flammable limits 1.2% (LEL) to 7.8% (UEL) by volume; flash point below 0 F; boiling point 80.08 C. Environmental: 'Benzene enters the environment from production, storage, transport, venting, and combustion of gasoline'.

title: CSB Safety Alert: Preventing High Temperature Hydrogen Attack (HTHA)
container: U.S. Chemical Safety and Hazard Investigation Board
verified_fact: HTHA 'severely cracked and weakened the carbon steel heat exchanger over time, leading to a rupture' (Tesoro Anacortes). 'American Petroleum Institute (API) Recommended Practice (RP) 941, Steels for Hydrogen Service at Elevated Temperatures and Pressures in Petroleum Refineries and the Petrochemical Plants. The standard uses Nelson Curves to predict the operating conditions where HTHA can occur in different types of steels.' 'the 2016 edition of API RP 941 reports 13 new failures below the carbon steel Nelson curve.' The CSB concluded inspection should not be relied on alone to control HTHA. CSB: the carbon steel Nelson curve 'has repeatedly proven to be unreliable'.
